question: Under Minnesota Statutes chapter 82, a person who, for compensation, lists, sells, exchanges, or negotiates the sale of real estate on behalf of another is defined as a:
choice_a: Real estate salesperson
choice_b: Closing agent
choice_c: Facilitator
choice_d: Real estate broker
explanation: Minn. Stat. § 82.55, subd. 19 defines "real estate broker" to include a person who, for compensation, lists, sells, exchanges, buys, rents, or manages real estate, or offers or attempts to negotiate such a transaction, for another.

question: Minnesota Statutes chapter 82 defines a "real estate salesperson" as a person who:
choice_a: Acts on behalf of a real estate broker in performing any act authorized by chapter 82
choice_b: Independently lists and sells real estate for compensation without broker supervision
choice_c: Holds an ownership interest in a licensed brokerage
choice_d: Is licensed solely to negotiate commercial leases
explanation: Minn. Stat. § 82.55, subd. 20 defines a real estate salesperson as one who acts on behalf of a real estate broker in performing any act authorized by chapter 82.

question: For purposes of Minnesota's real estate licensing statutes, the definition of "real estate" also includes:
choice_a: Any manufactured home, regardless of whether it is affixed to land
choice_b: A manufactured home, when it is affixed to land
choice_c: Only single-family detached residences
choice_d: Personal property fixtures unrelated to land
explanation: Minn. Stat. § 82.55, subd. 18 provides that "real estate" also includes a manufactured home when the manufactured home is affixed to land.

question: Under Minn. Stat. § 82.55, a "buyer's broker" is one who:
choice_a: Represents both buyer and seller equally without any written agreement
choice_b: Only provides transaction-facilitator services to a buyer
choice_c: Represents a purchaser under a signed agreement and owes the buyer fiduciary duties
choice_d: Represents the buyer only after the closing occurs
explanation: Minn. Stat. § 82.55, subd. 3a defines a "buyer's broker" as one representing a purchaser through a signed agreement, owing fiduciary duties to the buyer.

question: A "seller's broker" under Minnesota real estate law:
choice_a: Represents the buyer exclusively
choice_b: Has no fiduciary duty to the seller
choice_c: May only hold salesperson status, never broker status
choice_d: Represents the seller under a signed agreement and owes the seller fiduciary duties
explanation: Minn. Stat. § 82.55, subd. 23a defines a "seller's broker" as one representing a seller under a signed agreement, owing fiduciary duties to the seller.

question: Minn. Stat. § 82.55 defines "residential real property" as property that is:
choice_a: Occupied by, or intended to be occupied by, one to four families as their residence
choice_b: Any property zoned for residential use, regardless of the number of units
choice_c: Occupied exclusively by a single family
choice_d: Any property containing five or more dwelling units
explanation: Minn. Stat. § 82.55, subd. 23 defines residential real property as property occupied by, or intended to be occupied by, one to four families as their residence.

question: To apply for a Minnesota real estate broker's or salesperson's license, an applicant must be:
choice_a: At least 21 years of age at the time of making the application
choice_b: At least 18 years of age at the time of making the application
choice_c: At least 18 years of age at the time of licensure only, not application
choice_d: At least 19 years of age
explanation: Minn. Stat. § 82.58, subd. 1 requires applicants to be at least 18 years of age at the time of making application.

question: Which of the following must a Minnesota real estate salesperson license application include, among other things?
choice_a: Only a copy of the applicant's driver's license and the license fee
choice_b: A signed listing agreement with a client
choice_c: The applicant's legal name, age, residence address, the employing broker's information, and certificates of completion for courses I, II, and III plus passing exam results
choice_d: Proof of three years' sales experience in any industry
explanation: Minn. Stat. § 82.58, subd. 2 requires salesperson applications to state the applicant's legal name, age, and residence address, identify the employing broker, and include certificates of completion for courses I, II, and III along with passing exam results.

question: A person who passes the Minnesota real estate broker's examination must generally apply for the broker's license within:
choice_a: 30 days of passing the exam
choice_b: Five years of passing the exam
choice_c: There is no time limit to apply
choice_d: One year of passing the exam, unless the person maintains continuous active status as a licensed salesperson
explanation: Minn. Stat. § 82.58, subd. 3 gives an applicant who passes the broker exam one year to apply for licensure unless continuously active as a licensed salesperson, or reexamination is required.

question: A business entity applying for a Minnesota real estate broker license must:
choice_a: Have at least one individually licensed responsible person acting as broker for the entity
choice_b: Have every employee individually licensed as a broker
choice_c: Obtain a single entity license that authorizes any employee to act as a broker
choice_d: Be exempt from any individual licensing requirement
explanation: Minn. Stat. § 82.58, subd. 4 requires a business entity to have at least one individually licensed responsible person acting as broker; the entity license does not extend brokerage authority to other persons.

question: An applicant who passes the Minnesota real estate salesperson examination must file a license application within:
choice_a: Six months, with no exceptions
choice_b: One year, or reexamination is required
choice_c: 90 days, or the exam score is void
choice_d: Two years, matching the license renewal cycle
explanation: Minn. Stat. § 82.58, subd. 5 requires salesperson applicants to file their application within one year of passing the exam, or reexamination is required.

question: Under Minn. Stat. § 82.59, before receiving a Minnesota real estate license, each applicant must:
choice_a: Complete a one-year apprenticeship under a broker
choice_b: Obtain a four-year college degree in any field
choice_c: Pass an examination conducted by the commissioner
choice_d: Pass only a background check, with no examination
explanation: Minn. Stat. § 82.59, subd. 1 states that each applicant for a license must pass an examination conducted by the commissioner.

question: Under Minnesota law, an applicant whose real estate license was revoked within the past ___ is barred from sitting for the licensing examination.
choice_a: One year
choice_b: Five years
choice_c: Six months
choice_d: Two years
explanation: Minn. Stat. § 82.59, subd. 2 bars an applicant whose license was revoked within the preceding two years from taking the examination.

question: The Minnesota commissioner of commerce must offer the real estate licensing examination at least:
choice_a: Every 45 days
choice_b: Every 90 days
choice_c: Once per calendar year
choice_d: Every six months
explanation: Minn. Stat. § 82.59, subd. 3 requires the commissioner to conduct examinations at least every 45 days.

question: To sit for the Minnesota real estate broker's examination, absent a waiver, an applicant generally must show:
choice_a: Five years of experience as a licensed salesperson within the prior seven years
choice_b: Three years of experience as a licensed salesperson within the five years preceding application
choice_c: One year of experience as a licensed salesperson, with no further requirement
choice_d: Experience is never required if the applicant holds any college degree
explanation: Minn. Stat. § 82.59, subd. 4 requires broker applicants to demonstrate three years of experience as a licensed salesperson within the five years prior to application, absent a qualifying waiver.

question: The Minnesota commissioner may waive the broker license experience requirement for applicants who, among others:
choice_a: Have owned residential rental property for at least one year
choice_b: Have a relative who is a licensed broker
choice_c: Hold a real estate-related degree or are attorneys who practice real estate law
choice_d: Have completed only the 30-hour prelicensing course
explanation: Minn. Stat. § 82.59, subd. 5 allows the commissioner to waive the experience requirement for, among others, applicants with real estate degrees and attorneys who practice real estate law.

question: To pass the Minnesota real estate licensing examination, an applicant must score at least:
choice_a: 60% on either portion of the exam
choice_b: 70% on the uniform portion only
choice_c: 80% on the state portion only
choice_d: 75% on both the uniform and state portions of the exam
explanation: Minn. Stat. § 82.59, subd. 6 requires a score of 75% or higher on both the uniform and state exam portions; cheating disqualifies an applicant.

question: Under Minn. Stat. § 82.59, a Minnesota real estate salesperson applicant must complete:
choice_a: 30 hours of coursework before the exam and 60 hours after obtaining the license
choice_b: 60 hours of coursework before the exam and 30 hours after licensure
choice_c: 90 hours of coursework before the exam only
choice_d: No coursework, if the applicant passes the exam on the first attempt
explanation: Minn. Stat. § 82.59, subd. 8 requires salespersons to complete 30 hours of instruction before the exam and 60 hours after licensure (including fair housing and agency disclosure training).

question: Minnesota real estate salespersons and brokers must complete continuing education totaling:
choice_a: 15 hours per 24-month licensing period
choice_b: 30 hours per 24-month licensing period, with at least 15 hours completed in the first 12 months
choice_c: 30 hours every 12 months
choice_d: 45 hours per 24-month period
explanation: Minn. Stat. § 82.61(a) requires 30 hours of continuing education per 24-month period, with at least 15 hours completed in the first 12 months.

question: Under Minn. Stat. § 82.61, which subject matter may NOT be approved for Minnesota real estate continuing education credit?
choice_a: Fair housing law
choice_b: Agency disclosure law
choice_c: Motivation, salesmanship, psychology, or time management
choice_d: Real estate contract law
explanation: Minn. Stat. § 82.61(b) specifically excludes courses in motivation, salesmanship, psychology, or time management from continuing education approval.

question: Each continuing education period, a Minnesota real estate licensee must complete at least:
choice_a: Two hours on marketing techniques only
choice_b: One hour on property management only
choice_c: Three hours of any commissioner-approved elective, with no required topics
choice_d: One hour on agency representation/disclosure law and one hour on fair housing law
explanation: Minn. Stat. § 82.61(c) requires at least one hour each period on agency representation/disclosure laws and one hour on fair housing and anti-discrimination laws.

question: A Minnesota real estate license is valid for:
choice_a: 24 months, with new licenses expiring June 30 of the assigned expiration year
choice_b: 12 months from the date of issuance
choice_c: 36 months from the date of issuance
choice_d: An indefinite term, subject only to continuing education
explanation: Minn. Stat. § 82.63, subd. 5 sets a 24-month license term, with new licenses expiring June 30 of their assigned year.

question: Under Minn. Stat. § 82.63, a Minnesota real estate broker is:
choice_a: Only responsible for acts the broker personally directed in writing
choice_b: Responsible for the acts of any and all of the broker's salespersons and closing agents
choice_c: Not responsible for salesperson conduct once the salesperson is licensed
choice_d: Responsible only for salesperson conduct occurring at the broker's main office
explanation: Minn. Stat. § 82.63, subd. 3 makes the broker responsible for the acts of any and all of the broker's salespersons and closing agents.

question: A Minnesota real estate salesperson may:
choice_a: Be licensed under multiple brokers simultaneously if disclosed
choice_b: Act independently of any broker after two years of licensure
choice_c: Be licensed under only one broker at a time
choice_d: Choose to be licensed under a broker only for residential transactions
explanation: Minn. Stat. § 82.63, subd. 4 requires a salesperson to be licensed under one broker and prohibits representing multiple brokers simultaneously.

question: When a Minnesota real estate salesperson's employment with a broker terminates, the broker must notify the commissioner within:
choice_a: 30 days
choice_b: 24 hours
choice_c: 60 days
choice_d: Ten days
explanation: Minn. Stat. § 82.63, subd. 6 requires the broker to notify the commissioner within ten days of a salesperson's termination.

question: Under Minn. Stat. § 82.63, nonresidents of Minnesota:
choice_a: May obtain a Minnesota real estate license upon meeting all statutory requirements
choice_b: Are categorically barred from holding a Minnesota real estate license
choice_c: May only hold a Minnesota license if licensed as a broker in their home state
choice_d: May practice in Minnesota without any Minnesota license if licensed elsewhere
explanation: Minn. Stat. § 82.63, subd. 11 allows nonresidents to obtain a Minnesota license upon meeting all statutory requirements.

question: A Minnesota temporary broker's permit, issued during a broker emergency, is valid for:
choice_a: 90 days
choice_b: 45 days
choice_c: Six months
choice_d: One year
explanation: Minn. Stat. § 82.63, subd. 12 allows the commissioner to issue a temporary broker's permit valid for 45 days during a broker emergency.

question: Under Minn. Stat. § 82.57, the fee for an initial individual Minnesota real estate broker's license is:
choice_a: $70, with a $40 renewal fee
choice_b: $100, with a $150 renewal fee
choice_c: $150, with a $100 renewal fee
choice_d: $200, with no renewal fee
explanation: Minn. Stat. § 82.57 sets the initial individual broker's license fee at $150, with a $100 renewal fee (salesperson fees are $70 initial/$40 renewal).

question: Under Minn. Stat. § 82.75, real estate trust funds must be deposited in:
choice_a: The broker's personal checking account, clearly labeled
choice_b: A cash box maintained at the brokerage office
choice_c: An out-of-state financial institution only
choice_d: A bank, savings association, credit union, or industrial loan and thrift company
explanation: Minn. Stat. § 82.75, subd. 1 requires trust funds to be held in a bank, savings association, credit union, or industrial loan and thrift company.

question: Absent a written agreement otherwise, Minnesota law requires earnest money to be deposited into the listing broker's trust account within:
choice_a: Three business days of receipt of the funds or final acceptance of the purchase agreement, whichever is later
choice_b: 24 hours of receipt
choice_c: Ten business days of final acceptance
choice_d: One business day of receipt, regardless of acceptance status
explanation: Minn. Stat. § 82.75, subd. 5(c) requires deposit within three business days of receiving the funds or final acceptance of the purchase agreement, whichever is later, absent a different written agreement.

question: Minnesota's trust account law generally prohibits a broker from:
choice_a: Depositing any personal funds into the trust account under any circumstance
choice_b: Commingling personal or business funds with client trust account funds, except to cover service charges or minimum balance requirements
choice_c: Maintaining more than one trust account
choice_d: Using a trust account for closing agent funds
explanation: Minn. Stat. § 82.75, subd. 4 prohibits commingling of personal/business funds with trust funds, except personal funds designated to cover account service charges or minimum balance requirements.

question: Minnesota's trust account recordkeeping requirements obligate a broker to maintain records that include, among other things:
choice_a: Only the final closing statement for each transaction
choice_b: A single ledger showing total trust account funds with no per-transaction detail
choice_c: The date funds were received, their source, amounts, deposit dates, disbursement check numbers and dates, and monthly account balances
choice_d: Verbal confirmation logs of fund receipt
explanation: Minn. Stat. § 82.75, subd. 11 requires detailed records including date received, source, amount, deposit date, disbursement information, and monthly balances, kept separately per transaction/beneficiary.

question: Under Minnesota law, real estate trust funds may be disbursed only upon:
choice_a: The broker's sole discretion at any time
choice_b: Verbal instruction from either party
choice_c: Expiration of the listing agreement only
choice_d: Closing of the transaction, written agreement of the parties, court order, or a statutory affidavit under section 559.217
explanation: Minn. Stat. § 82.75, subd. 5(d) limits disbursement to closing, written party agreement, court order, or an affidavit under section 559.217.

question: When a purchase agreement does not specify disbursement timing, Minnesota law requires trust funds to be disbursed within:
choice_a: Ten business days after completion or termination of the transaction
choice_b: 30 calendar days after termination
choice_c: Immediately upon any party's request
choice_d: Five business days after the listing expires
explanation: Minn. Stat. § 82.75, subd. 5(d) requires disbursement within ten business days after transaction completion or termination when the agreement is silent on timing.

question: Under Minn. Stat. § 82.75, accrued interest on trust account funds (net of transaction costs), absent a different written agreement, is paid to:
choice_a: The listing broker as additional compensation
choice_b: The Minnesota Housing Finance Agency's housing trust fund
choice_c: The buyer at closing
choice_d: The real estate education, research and recovery fund
explanation: Minn. Stat. § 82.75, subd. 8 directs accrued interest, net of costs, to the Minnesota Housing Finance Agency's housing trust fund unless the parties agree otherwise in writing.

question: Under Minn. Stat. § 82.72, a real estate broker, salesperson, or closing agent must:
choice_a: Provide document copies only if requested in writing by a court
choice_b: Withhold document copies until closing to prevent disputes
choice_c: Provide parties with a true and accurate copy of any document pertaining to their interests
choice_d: Provide only a summary of transaction documents, not full copies
explanation: Minn. Stat. § 82.72, subd. 1 requires delivery of a true and accurate copy of any document pertaining to a party's interests.

question: The Minnesota commissioner's authority to examine broker records under Minn. Stat. § 82.72 extends to:
choice_a: Only records physically located within Minnesota
choice_b: Only records less than one year old
choice_c: Only records related to open, active transactions
choice_d: Examinations conducted outside Minnesota, at a reasonable time and scope
explanation: Minn. Stat. § 82.72, subd. 2 allows the commissioner to examine records at reasonable time and scope, including examinations conducted outside Minnesota.

question: Minnesota real estate brokers must retain listing, purchase agreement, and trust account records for:
choice_a: Six years from closing of the transaction (or the document's date if the transaction fails to close)
choice_b: Three years from the listing date
choice_c: Two years from closing
choice_d: Ten years from closing
explanation: Minn. Stat. § 82.72, subd. 3 requires six years of retention from closing, or from the document's date if the transaction fails to close.

question: Under Minn. Stat. § 82.72, required real estate transaction records:
choice_a: Must be kept only in original paper form
choice_b: May be stored by electronic means
choice_c: May never be digitized, due to trust account confidentiality
choice_d: Must be filed annually with the commissioner
explanation: Minn. Stat. § 82.72, subd. 4 expressly permits storage of required documents by electronic means.

question: After the required retention period expires, Minnesota brokers must dispose of real estate records using:
choice_a: Standard recycling, with no special procedure
choice_b: Immediate deletion, with no compliance standard
choice_c: Confidential record destruction procedures compliant with the Fair and Accurate Credit Transaction Act
choice_d: Procedures set by the buyer, not the broker
explanation: Minn. Stat. § 82.72, subd. 5 requires disposal using confidential record destruction procedures compliant with the Fair and Accurate Credit Transaction Act of 2003.

question: Under Minn. Stat. § 82.73, every Minnesota real estate office must maintain:
choice_a: A printed copy of every licensee's individual license only
choice_b: Only the broker's errors-and-omissions insurance policy
choice_c: A copy of the multiple listing service rules only
choice_d: Current copies of chapters 82 and 83 and their corresponding rules, which may be made available through an electronic agent
explanation: Minn. Stat. § 82.73, subd. 1 requires every office to maintain current copies of chapters 82 and 83 and their rules, accessible electronically.

question: Violating Minnesota's real estate standards of conduct under Minn. Stat. § 82.73 can result in:
choice_a: License denial, suspension, revocation, or censure
choice_b: Automatic criminal prosecution only
choice_c: A mandatory fine with no license action
choice_d: Loss of MLS membership only, with no state action
explanation: Minn. Stat. § 82.73, subd. 2 provides that violation of the standards of conduct can result in license denial, suspension, revocation, or censure.

question: Under Minn. Stat. § 82.73, a Minnesota broker must:
choice_a: Supervise only salespersons working at the broker's primary office
choice_b: Adequately supervise salespersons and employees, including monitoring listing agreements, purchase agreements, and trust account records, and designate an individual broker for each office location
choice_c: Delegate all supervisory duties to an office manager without oversight
choice_d: Supervise only transactions exceeding a certain dollar value
explanation: Minn. Stat. § 82.73, subd. 3(a) requires adequate supervision of personnel, including monitoring agreements and trust records, with a designated broker at each multi-location office.

question: Minn. Stat. § 82.73 makes the broker responsible for:
choice_a: Only documents the broker personally signs
choice_b: Documents only after the transaction closes
choice_c: The preparation, custody, safety, and accuracy of all real estate contracts, documents, and records
choice_d: Documents prepared by the buyer's attorney
explanation: Minn. Stat. § 82.73, subd. 3(b) places responsibility on the broker for preparation, custody, safety, and accuracy of all real estate contracts, documents, and records.

question: Under Minnesota's standards of conduct, a broker who investigates a complaint against a licensee must maintain the complaint file for:
choice_a: One year
choice_b: Six years, matching general record retention
choice_c: There is no retention requirement for complaint files
choice_d: Three years
explanation: Minn. Stat. § 82.73, subd. 3(c) requires brokers to investigate complaints and maintain complaint files for three years.

question: Under Minn. Stat. § 82.73, a broker is NOT required to supervise property management activities when:
choice_a: The real estate is individually or entity-owned by the licensee, who holds an ownership interest in it
choice_b: The property is managed remotely
choice_c: The property is commercial rather than residential
choice_d: The tenant is also a licensee
explanation: Minn. Stat. § 82.73, subd. 3(e) exempts a broker from supervising property management functions for property individually or entity-owned by the licensee who holds an ownership interest.

question: Under Minn. Stat. § 82.82, the commissioner may deny, suspend, or revoke a real estate license, or censure a licensee, when:
choice_a: Any single consumer complaint is filed, regardless of merit
choice_b: It is shown to be in the public interest and the licensee has engaged in prohibited conduct
choice_c: The licensee's license has been active for more than five years
choice_d: A competing broker requests it
explanation: Minn. Stat. § 82.82 authorizes discipline when both the public interest is served and the licensee has engaged in prohibited conduct.

question: One ground for Minnesota real estate license discipline under Minn. Stat. § 82.82 is:
choice_a: Failing to renew a license exactly on its expiration date
choice_b: Working part-time as a licensee
choice_c: Filing an incomplete application or a statement that is false or misleading in light of the circumstances
choice_d: Holding licenses in more than one state
explanation: Minn. Stat. § 82.82 lists filing an incomplete application, or a statement that is false or misleading, as a ground for discipline.

question: Minn. Stat. § 82.82 authorizes discipline against a licensee who engages in:
choice_a: Any advertising using the brokerage's own name
choice_b: Representing more than one buyer in a calendar year
choice_c: Attending continuing education courses late
choice_d: A fraudulent, deceptive, or dishonest practice
explanation: Minn. Stat. § 82.82 lists engaging in a fraudulent, deceptive, or dishonest practice as a ground for license discipline.

question: Under Minn. Stat. § 82.82, a broker may be disciplined for:
choice_a: Failing to reasonably supervise brokers, salespersons, or closing agents
choice_b: Supervising more than five salespersons at once
choice_c: Delegating trust account reconciliation to a licensed bookkeeper
choice_d: Operating more than one office location
explanation: Minn. Stat. § 82.82 lists failure to reasonably supervise brokers, salespersons, or closing agents as a disciplinary ground.

question: When the Minnesota commissioner summarily suspends a real estate license under Minn. Stat. § 82.82, the licensee is entitled to a hearing:
choice_a: Within 24 hours of the summary suspension
choice_b: Within 30 days of the summary suspension
choice_c: Only after the license's expiration date
choice_d: There is no right to a hearing after summary suspension
explanation: Minn. Stat. § 82.82 requires that a licensee whose license is summarily suspended be afforded a hearing within 30 days, conducted per chapter 14 procedures.

question: Under Minn. Stat. § 45.027, the commissioner of commerce may issue a:
choice_a: Criminal indictment without judicial involvement
choice_b: Order compelling a specific real estate transaction to close
choice_c: Cease and desist order requiring a person to stop violations, subject to a right to request a hearing
choice_d: Order requiring a licensee to change brokerages
explanation: Minn. Stat. § 45.027, subd. 5a authorizes the commissioner to issue cease and desist orders when evidence suggests unlawful conduct, with a right to request a hearing.

question: Under Minn. Stat. § 45.027, the commissioner of commerce may impose a civil penalty of up to:
choice_a: $1,000 per violation
choice_b: $50,000 per violation
choice_c: $500 per violation, capped at $2,000 total
choice_d: $10,000 per violation
explanation: Minn. Stat. § 45.027, subd. 6 allows the commissioner to impose a civil penalty of up to $10,000 per violation, unless a different statutory penalty applies.

question: Under Minn. Stat. § 45.027, the commissioner's investigative powers include the authority to:
choice_a: Subpoena witnesses, compel their attendance, and require production of books, papers, and records
choice_b: Only request voluntary written statements from licensees
choice_c: Search a licensee's home without a warrant
choice_d: Arrest a licensee suspected of fraud
explanation: Minn. Stat. § 45.027, subd. 2 grants subpoena authority to compel witness attendance and production of relevant books, papers, and records.

question: Under Minn. Stat. § 45.027, the commissioner may seek a(n) ___ in district court to enforce compliance with real estate laws.
choice_a: Eviction order
choice_b: Injunction
choice_c: Foreclosure judgment
choice_d: Arbitration award
explanation: Minn. Stat. § 45.027, subd. 5 allows the commissioner to seek an injunction in district court to enjoin violations and enforce compliance.

question: Minnesota's real estate education, research and recovery fund, established under Minn. Stat. § 82.86, is:
choice_a: A private fund administered by a state Realtor association
choice_b: Funded exclusively by state general tax revenue
choice_c: Administered by the commissioner of commerce to support education, research, and recovery for aggrieved persons with judgments against licensees
choice_d: Used only to pay commissioner's office salaries
explanation: Minn. Stat. § 82.86 establishes the fund, administered by the commissioner of commerce, to support education, research, and recovery for aggrieved persons who obtain judgments against licensees.

question: Under Minn. Stat. § 82.86, in addition to standard license fees, licensees contribute to the recovery fund:
choice_a: $100 for an initial license and $50 per renewal
choice_b: $10 for an initial license and $5 per renewal
choice_c: A flat $75 regardless of initial or renewal status
choice_d: $30 for an initial license and $20 per renewal period
explanation: Minn. Stat. § 82.86 sets recovery fund contributions at $30 for an initial license and $20 per renewal period, beyond standard fees.

question: Under Minn. Stat. § 82.86, the maximum recovery from the real estate recovery fund per claimant per transaction is:
explanation: Minn. Stat. § 82.86 caps recovery at $150,000 per claimant per transaction.

question: Regardless of the number of claims against a single Minnesota licensee, Minn. Stat. § 82.86 caps total recovery fund payouts related to that licensee at:
choice_d: There is no aggregate cap, only a per-claim cap
explanation: Minn. Stat. § 82.86 caps total fund payouts related to a single licensee at $250,000, regardless of claim quantity.

question: To recover from Minnesota's real estate recovery fund, a claimant must, among other things:
choice_a: Simply file a complaint with the commissioner, with no judgment required
choice_b: Show only that the licensee's license was later revoked
choice_c: Demonstrate fraudulent or deceptive practices, obtain a final court judgment, exhaust other remedies, and apply within one year of the judgment becoming final
choice_d: Obtain approval from the licensee's broker before filing
explanation: Minn. Stat. § 82.86 requires demonstrating fraudulent or deceptive practice, obtaining a final judgment, exhausting other remedies, and applying within one year of the judgment's finality.

question: When the Minnesota recovery fund pays a claim on behalf of a licensee, the licensee's license is:
choice_a: Immediately and permanently revoked, with no path to reinstatement
choice_b: Unaffected, since the fund payment satisfies the licensee's obligation
choice_c: Suspended only if the licensee fails to pay within ten years
choice_d: Automatically suspended until the licensee repays double the amount paid plus 12% interest and obtains a $40,000 surety bond
explanation: Minn. Stat. § 82.86 provides that recovery fund payments trigger automatic license suspension until the licensee repays double the amount plus 12% interest and obtains a $40,000 surety bond.

question: If the Minnesota recovery fund balance drops too low, the commissioner may impose an additional assessment on licensees not to exceed:
choice_a: $100 per renewal
choice_b: $500 per renewal
choice_c: $20 per renewal
choice_d: $1,000 per renewal
explanation: Minn. Stat. § 82.86 caps additional fund-replenishment assessments at $100 per renewal.

question: Under Minn. Stat. § 82.67, a real estate licensee must provide the agency disclosure form for one-to-four family residential transactions:
choice_a: Only at closing
choice_b: At the first substantive contact with the consumer
choice_c: Only if the consumer requests it in writing
choice_d: Within 72 hours after signing a purchase agreement
explanation: Minn. Stat. § 82.67 requires the agency disclosure form to be provided at the first substantive contact with the consumer in residential transactions involving one-to-four family homes.

question: Minnesota's agency disclosure form under Minn. Stat. § 82.67 must address which four relationship categories?
choice_a: Listing agent, selling agent, transaction coordinator, and closer
choice_b: Principal, agent, subagent, and customer
choice_c: Seller's broker, buyer's broker, dual agency, and facilitator
choice_d: Exclusive agency, open listing, net listing, and exclusive right to sell
explanation: Minn. Stat. § 82.67 requires the disclosure form to address seller's broker, buyer's broker, dual agency, and facilitator relationships.

question: Under Minnesota's agency disclosure requirements, dual agency (one broker representing both parties) is permitted only with:
choice_a: Verbal consent of either party
choice_b: Approval from the commissioner of commerce
choice_c: No consent needed if disclosed verbally
choice_d: Written consent of both parties
explanation: Minn. Stat. § 82.67 permits dual agency only with the written consent of both parties, requiring balanced treatment and confidentiality of price/terms unless otherwise instructed.

question: Under Minn. Stat. § 82.67, a "facilitator" broker generally:
choice_a: Owes no fiduciary duties except confidentiality, unless a written services agreement provides otherwise
choice_b: Owes full fiduciary duties identical to a seller's broker
choice_c: May not be used in Minnesota residential transactions
choice_d: Automatically becomes a dual agent
explanation: Minn. Stat. § 82.67 describes a facilitator as owing no fiduciary duties except confidentiality, unless a written services agreement specifies otherwise.

question: The fiduciary duties described on Minnesota's agency disclosure form include loyalty, obedience, disclosure, confidentiality, reasonable care, and:
choice_a: Guaranteeing a sale price
choice_b: Accounting for client funds
choice_c: Providing free legal advice
choice_d: Waiving inspection contingencies
explanation: Minn. Stat. § 82.67's disclosure form lists six fiduciary duties: loyalty, obedience, disclosure, confidentiality, reasonable care, and accounting for client funds.

question: When a consumer signs Minnesota's agency disclosure form, the signature acknowledges:
choice_a: Formation of a binding buyer's broker agreement
choice_b: Agreement to pay the broker's commission directly
choice_c: Receipt of the disclosure, which is not itself a representation contract
choice_d: Waiver of all fiduciary duties owed by the broker
explanation: Minn. Stat. § 82.67 requires the consumer's signature to acknowledge receipt and understanding that the disclosure is not a representation contract.

question: Under Minn. Stat. § 82.68, a licensee must affirmatively disclose, before negotiation or consummation of a transaction:
choice_a: The licensee's personal home address
choice_b: The broker's annual sales volume
choice_c: The identity of the brokerage's errors-and-omissions insurer
choice_d: The licensed name of the brokerage under which the licensee operates
explanation: Minn. Stat. § 82.68, subd. 1 requires affirmative disclosure of the licensed brokerage name before negotiation or consummation of a transaction.

question: Under Minn. Stat. § 82.68, when a principal in a transaction is a licensee, or a relative or business associate of the licensee, that fact must be:
choice_a: Disclosed in writing
choice_b: Disclosed verbally only
choice_c: Kept confidential to protect the licensee's privacy
choice_d: Disclosed only if the transaction later fails
explanation: Minn. Stat. § 82.68, subd. 2 requires written disclosure when a principal is a licensee or a relative or business associate of the licensee.

question: Minn. Stat. § 82.68 requires a licensee to disclose all material facts of which the licensee is aware that could adversely and significantly affect:
choice_a: The seller's personal finances
choice_b: The buyer's intended use of the property
choice_c: The listing broker's commission split
choice_d: The buyer's credit score
explanation: Minn. Stat. § 82.68, subd. 3 requires disclosure of all known material facts that could adversely and significantly affect a buyer's intended use of the property.

question: Under Minn. Stat. § 82.68, which of the following is specifically exempted from required material-fact disclosure in Minnesota?
choice_a: A known structural defect in the foundation
choice_b: An active insurance claim for roof damage
choice_c: That an occupant of the property had HIV/AIDS, or that a death occurred on the property
choice_d: A pending zoning change affecting the property
explanation: Minn. Stat. § 82.68, subd. 3 exempts disclosure of HIV/AIDS status of an occupant, deaths or perceived paranormal activity, and proximity to certain residential facilities.

question: Under Minn. Stat. § 82.68, if a licensee is notified that a party will not perform under a purchase agreement, the licensee must:
choice_a: Wait until the closing date to disclose the information
choice_b: Disclose only if asked directly by the other party
choice_c: Report the nonperformance solely to the commissioner
choice_d: Immediately inform the other parties to the transaction
explanation: Minn. Stat. § 82.68, subd. 4 requires immediate notice to the other parties when a licensee learns a party will not perform under the purchase agreement.

question: Under Minn. Stat. § 82.70, a real estate salesperson may accept a commission only from:
choice_a: The real estate broker to whom the salesperson is (or was, at the time of the transaction) licensed
choice_b: Any broker involved in the transaction
choice_c: The buyer directly, regardless of broker involvement
choice_d: A referring salesperson at another brokerage
explanation: Minn. Stat. § 82.70, subd. 1 limits salesperson compensation to the broker to whom the salesperson is or was licensed at the time of the transaction.

question: As a general rule, Minn. Stat. § 82.70 prohibits Minnesota licensees from paying or accepting compensation through:
choice_a: Any compensation whatsoever for a completed transaction
choice_b: Commission-splitting, rebates, referral fees, or finder's fees with unlicensed persons
choice_c: Compensation paid by check rather than wire transfer
choice_d: Referral fees paid between two licensed brokers
explanation: Minn. Stat. § 82.70, subd. 2 generally prohibits commission-splitting, rebates, referral fees, or finder's fees paid to or accepted from unlicensed persons, subject to narrow exceptions.

question: Under Minn. Stat. § 82.70, a timeshare referral fee paid to an unlicensed person is capped at:
explanation: Minn. Stat. § 82.70, subd. 2 caps timeshare referral fees at $150.

question: Under Minn. Stat. § 82.70, a resident referral fee for rental property is limited to:
choice_a: Two months' rent per referral
choice_b: A flat $500 per referral
choice_c: 10% of the annual lease value
choice_d: The value of one month's rent within a 12-month period
explanation: Minn. Stat. § 82.70, subd. 2 limits resident referral fees to the value of one month's rent within a 12-month period.

question: Minn. Stat. § 82.70 prohibits a licensee from accepting:
choice_a: Any undisclosed compensation or indirect remuneration connected to a principal's expenditures
choice_b: Any compensation from the listing broker
choice_c: A salary in lieu of commission
choice_d: Compensation for services rendered after closing
explanation: Minn. Stat. § 82.70, subd. 3 prohibits undisclosed compensation or indirect remuneration benefiting the licensee connected to a principal's expenditures.

question: Under Minn. Stat. § 82.70, a seller may authorize the seller's broker to:
choice_a: Withhold all compensation information from the buyer's broker
choice_b: Share compensation with other brokers, including a buyer's broker
choice_c: Pay compensation directly to the buyer
choice_d: Split compensation only with unlicensed referral sources
explanation: Minn. Stat. § 82.70, subd. 4 permits a seller to authorize the seller's broker to share compensation with other brokers, including a buyer's broker.

question: Under Minn. Stat. § 82.70, closing fees must be disclosed in writing to the parties at least:
choice_a: 30 days before settlement
choice_b: At the time the purchase agreement is signed
choice_c: One business day before settlement
choice_d: There is no advance disclosure requirement for closing fees
explanation: Minn. Stat. § 82.70, subd. 6 requires closing fees to be disclosed in writing at least one business day before settlement.

question: Under Minn. Stat. § 82.66, before advertising a property for sale or lease, a licensee must first obtain:
choice_a: Verbal permission from the seller
choice_b: Approval from the local MLS board
choice_c: A signed buyer's broker agreement
choice_d: A signed listing agreement or other signed written authorization
explanation: Minn. Stat. § 82.66, subd. 1a requires a signed listing agreement or other signed written authorization before advertising a property.

question: Under Minn. Stat. § 82.66, a Minnesota listing agreement may NOT include:
choice_a: Automatic extension or holdover clauses
choice_b: A definite expiration date
choice_c: The agreed commission rate
choice_d: A description of the property
explanation: Minn. Stat. § 82.66, subd. 1c prohibits automatic extension or holdover clauses in listing agreements.

question: Under Minn. Stat. § 82.66, a listing agreement's override (protection period) clause is enforceable only if the broker provides the seller a protective list of prospects within:
choice_a: 30 days of the listing's expiration
choice_b: 72 hours of the listing's expiration
choice_c: Immediately upon signing the listing
choice_d: Six months after expiration
explanation: Minn. Stat. § 82.66, subd. 1d requires a protective list within 72 hours of the listing's expiration for an override clause to be enforceable.

question: Minn. Stat. § 82.66's buyer's broker agreement requirements apply specifically to:
choice_a: Commercial transactions only
choice_b: All transaction types equally
choice_c: Residential transactions
choice_d: Transactions exceeding $1,000,000 in value
explanation: Minn. Stat. § 82.66, subd. 2f limits the buyer's broker agreement requirements of subdivision 2 to residential transactions.

question: Under Minn. Stat. § 82.69, any advertising by a Minnesota real estate licensee must:
choice_a: Include the licensee's personal license number only
choice_b: Be pre-approved by the commissioner before publication
choice_c: Exclude any mention of price
choice_d: Clearly and conspicuously display the real estate brokerage's name
explanation: Minn. Stat. § 82.69(a) requires advertising to clearly and conspicuously display the real estate brokerage name.

question: Under Minn. Stat. § 82.69, a licensee may use a team or group name in advertising only if:
choice_a: The primary broker authorizes the team name and the brokerage name is also clearly displayed
choice_b: The team has its own separate real estate license
choice_c: The team name replaces the brokerage name entirely
choice_d: The commissioner pre-approves the specific team name
explanation: Minn. Stat. § 82.69(b) permits team/group names only when authorized by the primary broker and the brokerage name is also clearly and conspicuously displayed.

question: Under Minn. Stat. § 82.81, a fundamental prohibition in Minnesota real estate law is that:
choice_a: Licensees may act as brokers for up to 90 days before licensure
choice_b: No person may act as a real estate broker or salesperson unless licensed
choice_c: Only brokers, not salespersons, need a license
choice_d: Unlicensed assistants may negotiate purchase price on a broker's behalf
explanation: Minn. Stat. § 82.81, subd. 1 prohibits any person from acting as a real estate broker or salesperson unless licensed.

question: Under Minn. Stat. § 82.81, a licensee may NOT delegate real estate work to an unlicensed person; specifically, a licensee may NOT:
choice_a: Employ a licensed closing agent
choice_b: Use an unlicensed administrative assistant to schedule showings
choice_c: Authorize an unlicensed individual to perform real estate services on the licensee's behalf
choice_d: Advertise jointly with another licensed broker
explanation: Minn. Stat. § 82.81, subd. 4 prohibits licensed professionals from authorizing unlicensed individuals to perform real estate services on their behalf.

question: Under Minn. Stat. § 82.81, a Minnesota licensee generally may NOT:
choice_a: Recommend a lender the party is free to decline
choice_b: Provide a list of several closing agents for the party to choose from
choice_c: Disclose an affiliated business arrangement
choice_d: Require a party to use a specific lender, attorney, or closing agent
explanation: Minn. Stat. § 82.81, subd. 8 prohibits requiring a party to use a specific lender, attorney, or closing agent.

question: Under Minn. Stat. § 82.81, a licensee may NOT:
choice_a: Discourage a party to a transaction from obtaining legal counsel
choice_b: Recommend that a party consult an attorney
choice_c: Refer a party to a list of local attorneys
choice_d: Advise a party to read the purchase agreement carefully
explanation: Minn. Stat. § 82.81, subd. 11 prohibits discouraging a party from obtaining legal counsel.

question: Under Minn. Stat. § 82.81, a licensee may NOT guarantee future profits to a party unless:
choice_a: The party is a first-time buyer
choice_b: The guarantee is fully disclosed in the contract
choice_c: The guarantee is verbal and informal
choice_d: Guarantees of future profit are never permitted under any circumstance
explanation: Minn. Stat. § 82.81, subd. 10 prohibits guaranteeing future profits unless fully disclosed in the contract.

question: Under Minn. Stat. § 82.81, when a transaction fails through no fault of the buyer, the listing broker generally:
choice_a: Automatically retains the full earnest money as a cancellation fee
choice_b: Must forward the earnest money to the recovery fund
choice_c: May not claim a portion of the purchaser's earnest money absent a separate agreement
choice_d: May retain the earnest money if the seller consents verbally
explanation: Minn. Stat. § 82.81, subd. 3 prohibits a listing broker from claiming a portion of the purchaser's deposit when the transaction fails through no fault of the buyer, absent a separate agreement.

question: Under Minn. Stat. § 82.81, specifically enumerated fraudulent practices include:
choice_a: Only acts involving forged signatures
choice_b: Only acts that result in a criminal conviction
choice_c: Acts committed exclusively by unlicensed persons
choice_d: Undisclosed dual representation and commingling of trust funds, among numerous other listed acts
explanation: Minn. Stat. § 82.81, subd. 12 enumerates sixteen specific acts constituting fraud, including undisclosed dual representation and commingling of funds.
